correctness.rationale: The proof fixes the hub and invokes a Schur complement with path polynomials P_m, giving det(xI-H)=(prod P_{ell-1})[x-sum (2P_{ell-2}+w)/P_{ell-1}]. Path parity makes the only non-odd rational terms sum_{odd s} W_s/P_{s-1}. These fractions have distinct leading powers x^{-(s-1)} at infinity; their constant-coefficient linear independence forces every W_s=0 separately. An odd-length cycle has gain weight w=1 or -2; hence W_s=k_s-3a_s. For each odd s the edgewise phase sum equals 2, yielding a=(2^s-2)/3, b=(2^{s+1}+2)/3 and the closed orientation product. Covers k>=1, repeated odd lengths, mixed lengths, and arbitrary even petals. Independent numerical direct Hermitian eigenspectrum enumeration of all 512 orientations of three triangles reproduced exactly 216 symmetric cases with spectral mirror error <=1.6e-15. Independent exact phase enumeration for lengths 3,5,7,9 and the three-pentagon formula 14520 agree. Finite checks corroborate; arbitrary-length sufficiency/necessity follows from the Schur complement and Laurent-order argument.

value.rationale: A one-vertex cactus bouquet is a natural first non-bipartite assembly family for sixth-root Hermitian spectral symmetry. The length-by-length cancellation theorem sharply characterizes existence, shows different odd lengths cannot compensate one another, and counts every labeled orientation. This is more than a routine single-triangle identity or a small enumeration: arbitrary cycle multiplicities and lengths are handled, with a natural graph-spectral reason to need the exact balance and counts.

final_claim: For a finite simple one-hub bouquet of cycles of lengths >=3 oriented with sixth-root Hermitian phase, spectral symmetry holds iff within every odd-length class s, one third of the k_s cycles have real gain -2 and two thirds have real gain +1; even cycles are unrestricted. Existence iff every odd k_s is divisible by 3; the labeled-orientation count is the exact lengthwise binomial/product formula in RESULT.md.
limitations: Only a finite simple one-hub cycle bouquet, labelled orientations, phase exp(iπ/3); not all cacti or other phase conventions. The general proof is analytic; small instances are corroboration only.
